title: Time-domain bitline sensing with shared TDCs on bonded logic wafer
idea: Box: pillar 1T1C x buried-channel access x time-domain sensing x CMOS-under-array x bulk Si x 28 nm logic wafer bonded. Each bitline's post-charge-share voltage starves a tiny inverter so the bit becomes a delay, and one time-to-digital converter serves 16 bitlines through a delay-line race, replacing 16 latch SAs with 16 inverters plus 1 TDC.
why: Periphery (~49% of die): SA stripe area -50-60%; time-domain gain stays cheap at low voltage, easing the voltage floor.

title: Nanoelectromechanical relay row decoders and wordline drivers above the array
idea: Box: stacked cap x vertical Si access x conventional SA x BEOL-over-array decoders x Si x MEMS sacrificial release. Row decode trees and 3 V wordline drivers are built as electrostatic NEM relays (TiN beams, air-gap release) in the upper metal levels; relays have zero off-leakage and tolerate 3-5 V, so thick-oxide HV transistors leave the silicon.
why: Row decoder/driver area moves off Si (periphery -10-15% of die); HV driver standby leakage ~0. Relay endurance (needs ~1e15 cycles) is the open risk.

title: Room-temperature single-electron transistor electrometer per bitline segment
idea: Box: 0.5 fF planar MIM cap x IGZO access x SET electrometer x local segment sensing x SOI x e-beam/DSA-defined dots. A silicon-nanowire quantum-dot SET (dot <5 nm, charging energy >> kT) at each 32-cell bitline segment turns a few hundred electrons of signal into a large current swing, so the cell no longer needs a 60:1 pillar capacitor.
why: Capacitor charge wall: Cs can drop ~10x (5 fF to 0.5 fF), deleting the high-AR etch; local gain also shortens bitlines.

title: Frequency-multiplexed resonator readout of 64 bitlines per receiver
idea: Box: trench cap x cryo-CMOS access x frequency-division readout x interposer-integrated resonators x sapphire-on-Si x high-Tc superconducting film. At 77 K each bitline ends in a high-Q LC resonator at a unique frequency whose varactor is detuned by the shared cell charge; one broadband LNA plus FFT reads 64 bitlines at once, like kinetic-inductance detector arrays.
why: Replaces 64 SAs with one receiver (SA area -90% for cryo data-center memory); cryo also stretches retention to minutes.

title: Time-domain reflectometry reads a whole gain-cell column in one pulse
idea: Box: 2T gain cell (storage node gates read FET) x read-FET loading x TDR echo sensing x controlled-impedance transmission-line bitline x Si x standard BEOL. With all read wordlines of a column enabled, each '1' cell's conducting read FET adds a shunt load at a known position, so one picosecond pulse's echo profile encodes every bit in the column by time of flight.
why: One TDR receiver per column instead of per-segment SAs; 256+ bits per pulse cuts sense energy and periphery count.

title: Spare array mats double as flying capacitors for wordline charge pumps
idea: Box: pillar caps x array access FETs as switches x no sensing x in-array power conversion x bulk Si x zero added masks. A few mats per bank wire their millions of 5 fF cell caps into parallel groups clocked as a switched-capacitor VPP/VBB pump, replacing the large planar MOS pump capacitors in the periphery.
why: Pump and decap area (several % of die) shrinks ~80% because cell caps are ~100x denser than MOS caps.

title: Bond array-only wafers to US mature-node periphery wafers
idea: Box: 1T1C x vertical-channel access x SA on a separate wafer x wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding at ~0.4 um pitch x two Si substrates x US 22-28 nm foundry. The memory fab builds pure arrays with no periphery or HV devices, and an existing U.S. logic foundry builds all SAs, decoders and pumps on a second wafer bonded face-to-face per bitline group.
why: Capital and U.S. manufacturability: periphery's ~49% moves to depreciated U.S. fabs; array die area ~-40%, DRAM-fab capex per bit down, domestic content up.

title: Complementary oxide-TFT sense amplifiers built in the metal stack
idea: Box: 1T1C x IGZO access x CMOS-TFT latch (n-IGZO + p-SnO) x monolithic over array x Si x 400 C sputter BEOL. Cross-coupled latches and column muxes are made as stacked oxide thin-film transistors directly over the cell array, so periphery stops competing for silicon area.
why: Periphery ~49%: die area -30-40% at the same capacity using non-EUV, low-temperature tools; p-type oxide mobility is the risk.

title: Time-interleaved high-speed sense amp serves eight bitlines
idea: Box: stacked cap x Si access x ADC-style time interleaving x analog mux plus isolation x bulk Si x FinFET periphery. After charge sharing, eight bitlines are isolated and hold their signals on their own parasitic capacitance while one fast, well-matched SA resolves them in ~1 ns slots through an analog mux and restores each in turn.
why: SA count /8 and SA stripe -60%; one large matched SA also lowers offset.

title: Floating-gate offset trim written into each sense amp at test
idea: Box: pillar cap x Si access x trimmed latch x planar x bulk Si x one added embedded-floating-gate mask. Each SA includes a small floating-gate transistor programmed at wafer sort to null its measured Vt mismatch, cutting input-referred offset from ~20 mV to ~2-3 mV.
why: Lower offset allows 2x longer bitlines (half the SAs, periphery -10% of die) or a 2x smaller Cs.

title: Resonant-tunneling-diode MOBILE latch replaces cross-coupled sense amp
idea: Box: stacked cap x Si access x NDR bistable sensing x heteroepitaxial devices under the bitline x Si x Si/SiGe RTD epitaxy. Two series resonant tunneling diodes clocked by a rising bias (monostable-bistable logic element) fall into one of two states set by a tiny bitline current imbalance, giving a 3-device latch with picosecond decisions.
why: SA area -60% and faster sensing; NDR supplies gain without large matched transistor pairs.

title: Steep-slope tunnel-FET sense amps for a 0.4 V array
idea: Box: low-voltage cap x Si access x TFET cross-coupled latch x CMOS co-integration x SOI x Ge/III-V source epitaxy. TFETs with 30-40 mV/decade subthreshold slope form a latch that resolves ~15 mV signals at 0.4 V supply, letting the array voltage drop from ~1 V to 0.4 V.
why: Voltage floor: bitline CV^2 energy ~-6x and sensing power down.

title: Negative-capacitance film cancels bitline parasitic capacitance
idea: Box: pillar cap x Si access x NC-compensated bitline x in-line HZO capacitor x Si x ALD ferroelectric. A stabilized negative-capacitance HZO element on the bitline subtracts most of its parasitic capacitance during charge sharing, raising the transfer ratio Cs/(Cs+Cbl) from ~0.1 toward ~0.4.
why: 3-4x more signal from the same 5 fF cell, so Cs can shrink (AR 60:1 toward 20:1) or bitlines can lengthen; attacks the capacitor wall.

title: Vertical CCD charge-shift columns with one floating-diffusion sense node
idea: Box: potential-well storage in poly-Si/IGZO channel x CCD transfer gates x floating-diffusion source follower x 3D vertical stack x Si x CMOS image-sensor fab. Bits are charge packets that shift up one tier per clock to a single sense node at the top, like an image sensor's vertical register, so tiers need no individual wordline decoders or staircase contacts.
why: 3D DRAM blocker plus periphery: per-tier decoders and staircases vanish; uses U.S. CIS fabs; suits page-oriented ~100 ns access.

title: Light-addressed wordlines with photoconductive access devices
idea: Box: stacked cap x photoconductive access (a-Si:H or MoS2) x electrical SA x bonded photonic layer x Si plus SiN waveguides x photonic foundry. Each row's access devices sit under a waveguide; a light pulse routed by an on-chip optical switch tree turns the row on, so no row decoders, 3 V wordline drivers or VPP pumps are needed, and dark access devices barely leak.
why: Periphery: row decode/drive area and wordline CV^2 energy removed; row hammer gone because there is no wordline coupling.

title: Stochastically assembled nanowire decoders with post-fab calibration map
idea: Box: crossbar-pitch storage x nanowire access x conventional SA x self-assembled sub-litho lines x Si x DSA patterning. A few lithographic mesowires address sub-lithographic lines through randomly doped regions, and a built-in calibration pass discovers each line's code and stores it in a lookup, so decoders need no litho pitch matching.
why: Decoders scale below litho pitch without EUV; decoder area ~-70% and fewer EUV layers.

title: Token-ring wordline selection for streaming-mode DRAM banks
idea: Box: pillar cap x Si access x standard SA x shift-register wordline selection x bulk Si x standard flow. In AI-weight and KV-cache streaming banks, a one-hot token passed along a shift register selects successive rows, with only coarse 64-row-block decoding for random jumps, replacing full in-pitch row decoders.
why: Row decoder area -70-80% in streaming banks; lower activation energy for sequential reads.

title: IGZO-isolated charge-transfer preamp enables 2048-cell bitlines
idea: Box: 1T1C x Si access x charge-transfer preamplifier x local isolation x bulk Si x BEOL IGZO switch. A gate-biased transfer transistor holds the bitline at a fixed potential while the cell charge is pushed onto a tiny sense node (gain ~Cbl/Csn ~10x), and an ultra-low-leakage IGZO switch isolates that node so the signal survives.
why: Bitlines 4x longer and SA count /4 (periphery ~-15% of die); bitline swing energy also drops.

title: Move DFT and BIST logic onto an active probe-card ASIC
idea: Box: any cell x any access x any SA x test logic off-die x bulk Si x probe-card ASIC. Built-in self-test engines, test-mode decoders and compression logic leave each DRAM die and live on a reusable active probe card that drives a minimal raw test port.
why: Periphery -2-4% per die forever, paid once per probe card; faster test too.

title: Weak canary bitlines trigger refresh only when decay is real
idea: Box: pillar cap x Si access x dedicated canary comparator x per-mat monitor x bulk Si x standard flow. Each mat carries a column of deliberately leaky cells (narrowed access gate) whose decay a reference comparator watches; that mat is refreshed only when the canaries cross threshold, tracking temperature and process automatically.
why: Refresh (~46 fJ/bit, 16-33% of idle power) cut 3-5x at typical temperatures; bandwidth loss down.

title: CFET-stacked sense amp transistors to halve SA stripe height
idea: Box: pillar cap x vertical-channel access x CFET-stacked latch x pitch-matched under bitline x bulk Si x sequential 3D integration. The NMOS and PMOS halves of each cross-coupled latch are stacked vertically as complementary FETs, so a full SA fits the bitline pitch of a 4F^2 array.
why: SA stripe height -50%, allowing 4F^2 arrays without SA pitch limits; periphery -10-15% of die.

title: Liquid-nitrogen DRAM with cryo-tuned long-bitline sense amps
idea: Box: smaller cap x Si access x cryo-optimized SA x LN2-immersed module x bulk Si x standard fab. At 77 K the subthreshold slope falls to ~20 mV/dec and mismatch narrows, so SAs resolve smaller signals; bitlines grow 4x and retention reaches hours, removing most refresh logic.
why: SA count /4 (periphery ~-20%) and refresh ~0; energy per bit lower even after cooling overhead in large AI pods.

title: Parametric varactor amplification boosts bitline voltage after charge sharing
idea: Box: stacked cap x Si access x parametric amplification x MOS-varactor bitline segments x bulk Si x standard. After the cell shares charge onto the bitline, a pump pulse drives MOS varactors on the bitline pair into depletion, shrinking capacitance so V = Q/C and the differential rise 3-5x before the latch fires: low-noise gain from capacitance modulation.
why: 3-5x more signal without more Cs: shrink the capacitor or lengthen bitlines.

title: Multi-threshold soft-sensing sense amps feed LDPC decoder in base die
idea: Box: shrunk 2.5 fF cap x Si access x 3-reference soft sensing x HBM base-die decoder x bulk Si x standard. Each SA compares against three references and ships a 2-bit log-likelihood value; a rate-0.89 LDPC decoder in the logic base die corrects a 1% raw cell BER to <1e-15 (BSC capacity at p=0.01 is ~0.92).
why: Tolerating 1% lets Cs halve (AR ~60:1 to ~30:1) and SA offset relax, for ~11% parity overhead.

title: Dead-zone sense amps flag uncertain bits as erasures, not errors
idea: Box: pillar cap x Si access x dual-offset comparator with dead zone x per-column flag bit x bulk Si x standard. Each SA has two skewed comparators; when they disagree the bit is marked erased, and since Reed-Solomon corrects twice as many erasures as unknown errors, a 1% raw BER that is mostly flagged costs only ~4-6% parity.
why: Absorbs 1% cell BER with less code overhead than blind ECC, so SAs and Cs can shrink.

title: Refresh interval set by 1% failure point, scrubbed by ECC
idea: Box: standard cap x Si access x SA plus decode-on-refresh x controller scrub x bulk Si x standard. Retention is specified where 1% of cells fail instead of at the 1e-9 tail, which stretches refresh ~16-30x; each refresh pass reads through the decoder and writes back corrected data so errors never pile up.
why: Refresh energy (16-33% of idle) and bandwidth loss (10-20%) cut >90%; the ~13 fA leakage tail stops mattering.

title: Three-transistor single-ended sense amp with 60 mV offset accepted
idea: Box: pillar cap x Si access x single-ended skewed-inverter sensing x minimum-size SA x bulk Si x standard. The 8-10 transistor cross-coupled, equalized SA becomes a precharged skewed inverter plus a restore transistor that tolerates ~60 mV offset, so ~1% of bits mis-sense and are fixed downstream.
why: SA area -60%: the SA stripe falls from ~10% to ~4% of die and matched-pair layout rules disappear.

title: Triple bitline length to 1536 cells, accept 1% signal failures
idea: Box: standard cap x Si access x standard SA x long-bitline mats x bulk Si x standard. Cut the number of SA stripes ~3x by hanging 1536 cells per bitline; the lower transfer ratio leaves ~1% of weak cells unreadable, and the code absorbs them.
why: Periphery: SA stripes -65% (~10% of die area), cost per bit ~-10%.

title: Delete redundancy rows, columns and fuse banks; ECC absorbs defects
idea: Box: standard cell x Si access x standard SA x no repair periphery x bulk Si x shorter test flow. Defects and weak cells up to a 1% budget stay in place under the code, so spare rows and columns, redundancy compare logic, laser/e-fuse banks and repair test steps all go.
why: Periphery -3-5% of die, lower test cost and time, higher yield because defects stop scrapping dies.

title: Bit-significance mats: AI weight LSBs on cheap unprotected mats
idea: Box: mixed caps x Si access x two SA grades x bit-plane-split mats x bulk Si x standard. Model weights are stored bit-plane-sliced: MSB planes go to mats with full ECC, while LSB planes go to long-bitline, small-SA, rarely refreshed mats where 1% flips move a value by <0.4% of range, which inference ignores.
why: Unequal error protection: ~60% of bits live on mats with ~40% less periphery and ~10x less refresh.

title: Multi-row OR-sensing reads sparse zero blocks in one activation
idea: Box: pillar cap x Si access x threshold-OR sensing x 8-wordline simultaneous activation x bulk Si x standard. For sparse activations and pruned weights, eight rows open at once and the SA only asks whether any charge is present (group testing); all-zero groups are confirmed with one sense instead of eight, and the extra multi-row disturb (<1%) is tolerated.
why: Sense energy and overfetch for sparse data cut up to 8x, spending the 1% budget on multi-row disturb.

title: Half-volt array: 0.5 V VARY with 1% sensing failures
idea: Box: standard cap x Si access x high-gain SA x low-voltage array domain x bulk Si x standard. Bitline/cell voltage drops from ~1 V to 0.5 V and the wordline from ~3 V to ~2.2 V; the halved signal mis-senses ~1% of bits, which the code repairs.
why: Voltage floor: array CV^2 energy ~-4x, smaller pumps, less wordline stress.

title: Drop row-hammer counters; let flips land inside ECC budget
idea: Box: standard cap x Si access x standard SA x no TRR or counter logic x bulk Si x standard. Target-row-refresh trackers and per-row activation counters are removed; a randomized background scrub plus the 1%-capable code absorb hammer flips, and a simple activation-rate cap keeps them under 0.1% of a codeword.
why: Periphery: row-hammer tracker SRAM and logic (growing as the threshold falls to ~1k) removed, with code margin as the defense.

title: Display-fab glass panels manufacture DRAM periphery at Gen-8.5 scale
idea: Box: Si array die x Si access x LTPS/IGZO sense amps x panel-level bonding x glass substrate x display fab. Sense amps, decoders and pumps are made as high-variability LTPS/oxide TFT circuits on large glass panels in under-used display fabs and bonded to array-only dies; the 1% budget absorbs TFT Vt scatter.
why: Capital intensity: display area costs ~1/50 of 300 mm logic per m^2; frees DRAM-fab capacity and adds a new supply base.

title: DUV-only arrays with loose CD control, weak-cell tail coded away
idea: Box: pillar cap x Si access x soft-decision SA x standard integration x bulk Si x ArF-immersion SAQP without EUV. Critical layers are patterned with DUV multipatterning at wider CD variation, letting ~1% of cells be too weak or leaky; soft sensing plus the code covers them.
why: EUV layers drop from 5-7 to 0, cutting capex and single-supplier dependency; wafer cost ~-20%.

title: Two-bit-per-cell DRAM with Gray-coded four-level sensing
idea: Box: high-k pillar cap x Si access x 4-level successive-approximation sensing x standard x bulk Si x standard. Each cell stores one of four charge levels read by a 2-step SAR comparator; Gray mapping makes most level errors single-bit, so the ~1% raw error rate fits a rate-0.88 code.
why: Density: 2 bits per cell gives ~1.75x bits per mm^2 after parity, with no new lithography.

title: Rescue rejected DRAM dies behind a strong-ECC buffer controller
idea: Box: existing dies x existing access x existing SA x ECC buffer chip on module x existing substrate x existing fabs. Buy dies that fail JEDEC bins with <=1% bad bits at scrap prices and package them on modules or CXL cards whose buffer chip runs LDPC plus remapping, sold as a new grade.
why: Usable supply rises right away (recapturing yield loss of a few to 10%) with zero new fabs; cost per bit down.

title: Standardize a raw-tolerant DRAM grade with soft-bit interface
idea: Box: any cell x any access x soft-output SA x host-side decoding x any substrate x any fab. Push a JEDEC-style spec, backed by CHIPS-funded qualification, for 'RT-DRAM' rated at 1% raw BER that exposes soft bits and moves ECC into the host or CXL controller, so suppliers can sell relaxed dies interchangeably.
why: Policy unlocks the relaxed-cell gains industry-wide and lets new U.S. entrants compete on cheaper relaxed processes.

title: Truncated restore: shorten write-back, accept 1% under-restored cells
idea: Box: standard cap x Si access x early-terminated restore x standard x bulk Si x standard. After the destructive read the SA stops restoring at ~70% of full level, cutting tRAS/tRC ~30%; the few cells left too weak for the next read fall inside the code budget, and refresh tops them up.
why: Destructive-read cost: row cycle time ~-30%, higher bank throughput, less energy per activation.

title: Analog syndrome bitlines compute parity by charge summation in-array
idea: Box: pillar cap x Si access x multi-level analog-sum sensing x dedicated parity bitline x bulk Si x standard. During activation, cells of a parity group also dump charge onto a shared parity bitline; a small multi-level comparator turns the summed charge into a count whose mod-2 is the syndrome, so only words with a nonzero syndrome go to the full decoder.
why: Decoder power and latency at 1% BER: most words skip decoding; periphery ECC logic ~-50%.

title: Bit-flip-aware training lets LLM caches run with zero ECC
idea: Box: cheapest cell x Si access x minimal SA x no ECC x bulk Si x standard. Models are trained and quantized with 1% random bit-flip injection on weights and KV-cache (bit-flip dropout, clamped exponent bits), then stored in uncoded relaxed DRAM where 1% flips act as regularization noise.
why: Removes all ECC parity and decode logic for AI tiers: +12% capacity and lower latency on top of relaxed-cell savings.

title: Latch resolution time as free confidence signal for decoding
idea: Box: pillar cap x Si access x metastability-timed latch x per-SA time comparator x bulk Si x standard. A tiny counter measures how long each latch takes to resolve; slow resolution (small input) marks the bit low-confidence, giving the decoder soft information without extra reference reads.
why: Soft decoding of 1% raw BER at single-read latency; near-capacity code rates (~0.9) at almost no area.

title: Few-electron planar cells with local two-transistor segment preamps
idea: Box: 0.3 fF planar MIM cap x IGZO access x local 2T gain preamp per 16 cells x monolithic BEOL x Si x no high-AR etch. Each cell stores ~1,800 electrons on a flat capacitor, a local preamp at each 16-cell segment amplifies it, and the ~1% errors from shot noise and leakage scatter are corrected by the code.
why: Capacitor charge wall: removes the 60-75:1 pillar entirely and can be stacked in BEOL tiers for 3D.

title: Stack-level erasure coding rescues HBM stacks with one weak die
idea: Box: standard cells x Si access x per-die soft SA x cross-die erasure code in base die x Si x TSV stacking. Each codeword is spread across all 12-16 dies of an HBM stack, so a die with ~1% bad cells or a weak TSV group counts as a partial erasure instead of scrapping the stack.
why: HBM TSV tax: most of the 20-30% stack yield loss recovered; effective HBM supply +15-25%.

title: Run DRAM hot at 105 C without double-rate refresh
idea: Box: standard cap x Si access x temperature-aware soft SA x dense hot packaging x bulk Si x standard. The array may run at 105 C on base refresh; thermally accelerated leakage pushes raw BER up to ~1%, the code absorbs it, and packages can sit closer to accelerators.
why: Energy: removes refresh doubling and some cooling; tighter co-packaging cuts data-movement pJ/bit.

title: Open-bitline 4F^2 vertical cells, coupling noise absorbed by code
idea: Box: vertical-channel 4F^2 cell x VCT access x open-bitline SA without dummy mats x tight-pitch array x bulk Si x standard. Accept the higher bitline-to-bitline coupling noise and weaker reference symmetry of open-bitline 4F^2 arrays, and delete edge dummy mats, letting ~1% of reads fail and be corrected.
why: Density: 6F^2 to 4F^2 (+50% bits per area) and no dummy-mat overhead (~3-5%).
